findings.claim: In addGuests.handler.ts, the team permission check uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` where `||` is intended. This reduces it to an owner-only check, so team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`; isTeamAdmin matches ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284) while isTeamOwner matches only OWNER (286-295), so the conjunction is owner-only and a team ADMIN who is neither organizer nor attendee hits the FORBIDDEN throw at line 54-55.

findings.claim: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check lowercases the blacklist but compares it against the raw guest email, with no toLowerCase or extractBaseEmail normalization. Blacklisted addresses therefore pass when submitted with different casing or a plus-alias.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 lowercases the blacklist entries but calls `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` on the raw guest string, and addGuests.schema.ts:5 (`z.array(z.string().email())`) does no lowercasing or base-email normalization. Other call sites such as packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:742-743 use `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()`, so a differently cased or plus-aliased blacklisted address passes here.

findings.claim: De-duplication against existing booking attendees is case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to an existing `a@x.com`.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 filters with strict `guest === attendee.email`, and addGuests.schema.ts:5 (`z.array(z.string().email())`) never lowercases the input; the Attendee model (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:526-539) has no unique or case-insensitive constraint on email, so `A@x.com` is inserted alongside an existing `a@x.com`.

findings.claim: The server does not de-duplicate the input guests array (uniqueGuests only filters existing attendees and the blacklist). A direct tRPC call with repeated emails creates duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate emails, and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no server-side cap on list size.

verifier.reason: The server schema is just `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refine or max length (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5); the handler's `uniqueGuests` only filters existing attendees and the blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) and feeds `createMany` (addGuests.handler.ts:92-106), while `Attendee` has only non-unique indexes on email and bookingId (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:537-538). Repeated emails in a direct call therefore create duplicate attendee rows, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends one email per attendee row (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:232-240); the uniqueness check exists only client-side in AddGuestsDialog.tsx.

findings.claim: The handler passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`. As a result, existing or filtered attendees are classified as new and receive the wrong email (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail), and notifications go to guests who were not actually added.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 passes raw `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests` (line 74), and packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541-542 sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to any attendee in that list, so an existing attendee re-submitted alongside a new guest gets the wrong email. The claim's last clause is overstated: emails only go to `calendarEvent.attendees`, so blacklisted guests who were never added receive nothing.

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails does not check the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata. Emails are therefore sent even when standard host/attendee emails are disabled.

verifier.reason: `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` at packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550 takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and sends organizer, team-member and attendee emails unconditionally, unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails` just above it (lines 495-524), which gates on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. The handler calls it as `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 without passing `booking.eventType?.metadata`.

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect the hideCalendarNotes setting, so hidden notes can be sent to attendees.

verifier.reason: `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550) passes the event to `AttendeeScheduledEmail`/`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` with no `hideCalendarNotes` masking, unlike `sendScheduledEmails` at :119.
